x: Ted Jackman and Jim Latter had a determined struggle for second place, but Latter's earlier efforts in catching the leaders had sapped his strength, and Jackman was able to draw away in the last hundred yards.

Our junior sprinters once again demonstrated their worth by taking first three places in the 100 yards. The Walk was won by Ted Jackman. still improving; and Ring cleverly won the Mile handicap from R.

The war has been responsible for bringing many of our older members out of retirement, and in this respite we welcome back, among others: Charlie Redgrave, Jarvis Boddington, Willis, Ted Jackman, and Goold.

Spent a week-end at a French resort to which the Plymouth meeting seemed "like a baby show." To quote him further: "Vive L'Entente Cordiale!" Ted Jackman, transferred to Portsmouth (N.F.S.). Has recently been up to town for an operation on his foot.
Ted Jackman hopes to be on the road again after having had treatment for foot trouble. Bert Lindsey is another who works long and inconvenient hours, but he occasionally manages a run from the Hall.
It is with the greatest regret that we have to announce the death of TED JACKMAN at the early age of 35 years. Ted joined us in 1930 and quickly showed that he had walking ability.
